KM1Zj77x6jyW9VsInPz3.description:
Ralligold GR from Tata Rallis is a granular mycorrhizal biofertilizer. Mycorrhizal fungi live on plant roots and spread fine threads into the soil, so the crop can reach phosphorus, water and micronutrients that its own roots cannot. The result farmers look for is a stronger root system, better use of the fertilizer already applied, and a crop that copes better with dry spells.

Because it is a granule, Ralligold GR goes into the soil near the root zone: at sowing or transplanting, or along the rows in standing crops, mixed with sand, soil or compost so it spreads evenly. It suits most field crops, vegetables and fruit crops, including tomato, chilli, potato, cotton, maize, wheat, onion, soybean, pulses, sugarcane, ginger, turmeric, banana, grapes, pomegranate and citrus.

As a biological product it works best in moist soil with organic matter. Keep the pack sealed in a cool, shaded place and use it before the expiry date printed on the bag, since the fungal spores are alive.

faqs.q: How much Ralligold GR should I use per acre?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives 4 kg per acre for most field crops and vegetables, and 8 kg per acre for long-duration crops such as sugarcane, ginger, turmeric and banana. Follow the rate on your pack, as it can differ by crop.
At sowing or transplanting, placed close to the seed or root zone, or along the rows early in the crop. The fungi need to reach young roots to colonise them.

faqs.q: Can I mix Ralligold GR with chemical fertilizers?
faqs.a: It can go into soil that has received normal fertilizer, but do not mix it in the same bag or tank with fungicides, which can harm the living fungi. Apply fungicide seed treatments and soil drenches separately.

faqs.q: Is it the same as a phosphate fertilizer?
faqs.a: No. It adds no phosphorus itself; it helps roots take up the phosphorus that is already in the soil or that you apply.

jhXloji8VeTbqLwNku3c.description:
Adama 2,4-D is a selective, systemic herbicide based on 2,4-D, one of the most widely used weed killers for broadleaf weeds. It is absorbed through the leaves, moves through the weed and disturbs its growth hormones, so susceptible weeds twist, stop growing and die over one to two weeks. Grasses and cereal crops are much less sensitive to it, which is why 2,4-D is used to clean broadleaf weeds out of crops such as wheat, maize, sorghum and sugarcane.

Spray it after the weeds have emerged and while they are young and actively growing. Use a flat-fan nozzle, spray on a calm day, and keep the spray away from sensitive broadleaf crops such as cotton, tomato, chilli, grapes and pulses: even a little drift can damage them.

The dose and the right crop stage are printed on the label for each crop. Wear gloves and a mask while mixing and spraying, and do not use the same pump for insecticide or fungicide sprays on sensitive crops without washing it thoroughly.

faqs.a: Broadleaf weeds such as Chenopodium (bathua), Convolvulus, Parthenium and many other dicot weeds. It does not control grassy weeds.

faqs.q: In which crops can I use it?
faqs.a: In crops where it is registered on the label, typically cereals such as wheat and maize, and sugarcane. Never spray it on cotton, vegetables, pulses or fruit crops.
Follow the crop-specific dose and water volume on the Adama label. The rate depends on the crop and the weed stage.

faqs.q: How soon will I see results?
faqs.a: Leaves start to curl and twist within a few days; weeds usually die in one to two weeks.

CtVwXhQFGN30lyRraK1X.description:
Alika from Syngenta is an insecticide that combines two actives: thiamethoxam 12.6% and lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% in a ZC (mixed capsule suspension) formulation. Thiamethoxam is systemic: the plant takes it up and it protects new growth against sucking pests such as jassids, aphids, whiteflies and thrips. Lambda-cyhalothrin acts on contact and gives a quick knockdown of chewing pests such as caterpillars and bollworms.

That pairing makes Alika useful when a crop has sucking and chewing pests at the same time, for example in cotton, maize, soybean, chilli and tomato. The ZC formulation releases part of the lambda-cyhalothrin quickly and part over time, so control lasts longer than with a simple EC.

Spray at the first sign of pest build-up, with good coverage of both leaf surfaces. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label, and avoid spraying when bees are active, as both actives are toxic to bees.

faqs.a: Thiamethoxam 12.6% plus lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC.
Sucking pests such as jassids, aphids, thrips and whiteflies, and chewing pests such as caterpillars and bollworms, in the crops listed on its label.

faqs.q: What is the dose per acre?
faqs.a: It depends on the crop. Follow the dose, water volume and waiting period printed on the Syngenta label for your crop.
No. Both actives are toxic to bees. Do not spray on flowering crops while bees are foraging; spray in the evening if needed.

BXKtdthy1YdPldbgohc1.description:
Glo-It is a fungicide from Syngenta for paddy (rice). It combines two triazole fungicides, propiconazole 13.9% and difenoconazole 13.9%, in an EC (emulsifiable concentrate) formulation that mixes with water to form a milky spray. Both actives are systemic: the plant absorbs them and moves them within the leaf and sheath, where they stop the fungus from making ergosterol, a building block of its cell membrane. This gives protection to healthy tissue and also checks infections that have only just started.

Glo-It is used mainly against two diseases of paddy. Sheath blight shows as oval, greyish-green patches with brown edges on the leaf sheath near the water line, which spread upwards and can make the crop lodge. Dirty panicle, or grain discoloration, turns grains brown or black and lowers their market value. For sheath blight, spray when the first patches appear, usually from the tillering stage, and direct the spray towards the lower part of the plants. For dirty panicle, the spray around booting to early panicle emergence matters most.

Use the dose, water volume and number of sprays printed on the label, and observe the waiting period before harvest. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask while mixing and spraying, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: Propiconazole 13.9% plus difenoconazole 13.9% EC. Both are systemic triazole fungicides.

faqs.q: Which diseases does Glo-It control in paddy?
faqs.a: Sheath blight and dirty panicle (grain discoloration), as per its label.

faqs.q: When should I spray Glo-It on paddy?
faqs.a: At the first sign of sheath blight patches, usually from tillering, and again around booting to early heading to protect the grain from discoloration. Follow the number of sprays and the waiting period on the label.
Follow the dose and water volume printed on the Syngenta label for paddy. Using more than the label rate does not give better control.

sources: Albaugh India product page for the same active combination

kj9BFK4YdimiVaZlUEtn.description:
This pack holds onion seed of Phule Samarth (also written Fule Samarth), a red onion variety released in 2004 by Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Rahuri, and sold here under the Red King name. The seller describes it as a red onion with an attractive colour, grown both for bulbs and for green onion leaves (kanda paat).

Published descriptions of Phule Samarth from MPKV and ICAR give its main traits: dark red bulbs that are globular and round, with a thin neck, maturing about 100 to 110 days after transplanting, and medium keeping quality. It is recommended for the kharif and early rabi (rangda) seasons, and the average yield reported for it is about 200 to 250 quintals per hectare. Because its keeping quality is medium, it suits farmers who plan to sell within a few months rather than store the bulbs for long.

Raise seedlings on raised nursery beds with fine, well-drained soil, and transplant healthy seedlings when they are six to eight weeks old. Keep the field weed-free in the early weeks, avoid waterlogging in the kharif season, and watch for thrips and purple blotch. The pack size is 1 kg. Check the variety name, lot number and germination details printed on the packet before sowing.

faqs.q: In which season can I grow Phule Samarth onion?
faqs.a: MPKV and ICAR describe it as a variety for the kharif and early rabi (rangda) seasons.

faqs.q: How long does it take to mature?
faqs.a: About 100 to 110 days after transplanting.

faqs.q: What do the bulbs look like?
faqs.a: Dark red, globular and round, with a thin neck.

faqs.q: Can I store the bulbs for a long time?
faqs.a: Its keeping quality is described as medium, so plan to sell within a few months. For long storage, rabi-season storage varieties are better suited.

faqs.q: Can I use it for green onions?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller says it is used for both bulbs and green onion leaves (kanda paat).

sources: ICAR Indian Horticulture variety description (Phule Samarth)

dC3JogwQI7uGAORqApuM.description:
Fusiflex from Syngenta is a selective post-emergence herbicide for soybean and other broadleaf crops. It combines two actives that cover each other's gaps: fluazifop-p-butyl, which kills grassy weeds by stopping fat production in the grass, and fomesafen, which burns down broadleaf weeds by disrupting their cell membranes. One spray therefore controls both grasses and broadleaf weeds in the crop.

The best time to spray is when the weeds are young, at the two to four leaf stage, and the crop is in its early growth. Use clean water and a flat-fan nozzle for even cover, and do not spray before rain. Fusiflex is used in soybean in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, where it is one of the common weed-control sprays in kharif.

Use the dose and water volume given on the Syngenta label, and do not spray it on cereal crops such as maize, wheat or rice, which are grasses and will be damaged.

faqs.a: Mainly soybean, and other broadleaf crops listed on its label. It must not be used on maize, wheat, rice or other cereal crops.
Grassy weeds such as Echinochloa and Digitaria, and broadleaf weeds such as Commelina, Digera and Amaranthus, when sprayed at the young stage.
Post-emergence, when weeds have two to four leaves. Older weeds are harder to kill.
Follow the dose and water volume printed on the Syngenta label for your crop.

PvvTdzZEvxaBEIUyirrR.description:
Tata Metri from Rallis India contains metribuzin 70% WP, a selective systemic herbicide. Metribuzin is taken up by both roots and leaves and blocks photosynthesis in susceptible weeds, which turn yellow and die. It controls many annual broadleaf weeds and some annual grasses, and it is used in crops such as soybean, potato, tomato, wheat and sugarcane, depending on the label.

Metribuzin can be applied before the weeds come up (pre-emergence) or soon after (early post-emergence), as the label for each crop specifies. Applied to moist soil, it forms a weed-free layer that stops new flushes for several weeks. Light, sandy soils with little organic matter need extra care, because the active moves faster and can harm the crop.

The 100 g pack suits small plots. Mix the powder in a little water first, then fill the tank. Follow the crop-specific dose and timing on the Rallis label, and wear gloves and a mask while mixing.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Tata Metri?
faqs.a: Metribuzin 70% WP (wettable powder).

faqs.q: In which crops can Tata Metri be used?
faqs.a: In the crops listed on its label, such as soybean, potato, tomato, wheat and sugarcane. Check the label before using it on any other crop.

faqs.q: Should I spray it before or after the weeds come up?
faqs.a: It works as a pre-emergence or early post-emergence herbicide depending on the crop. Follow the timing on the label for your crop.
It depends on the crop and soil type. Use the dose on the Rallis label; lower rates are usually advised on light soils.

Hy4dLsiPmHkHfCTDHYtX.description:
Weedmar Super from Dhanuka is a selective post-emergence herbicide containing 2,4-D amine salt 58% SL. It controls broadleaf weeds and sedges in cereal crops and sugarcane. The amine salt is absorbed through the leaves and moves through the weed to its growing points, where it upsets the plant's hormone balance; affected weeds twist, stop growing and die over one to two weeks.

Weedmar Super is commonly used in wheat, maize, sorghum, rice and sugarcane to clean up broadleaf weeds such as bathua (Chenopodium), Convolvulus and Parthenium, and sedges such as Cyperus. Spray when the weeds are young and actively growing, on a calm day, with a flat-fan nozzle.

Keep it well away from broadleaf crops such as cotton, vegetables, grapes and pulses, which are very sensitive to 2,4-D drift. Follow the dose and timing printed on the Dhanuka label for your crop.

faqs.a: 2,4-D amine salt 58% SL.

faqs.q: Which crops can I spray it on?
faqs.a: Cereal crops such as wheat, maize, sorghum and rice, and sugarcane, as listed on the label.
No. It controls broadleaf weeds and sedges. Grassy weeds need a different herbicide.

faqs.q: Is it safe near cotton or vegetables?
faqs.a: No. Even small amounts of drift can damage cotton, vegetables, grapes and pulses. Spray only on calm days and keep a safe distance.

wrhEtw0k4nvEypl7EkUt.description:
Tizom is a sugarcane herbicide from Dhanuka Agritech, developed with Nissan Chemical Corporation of Japan and launched in 2023. It combines halosulfuron methyl 6% and metribuzin 50% WG. Halosulfuron is one of the few actives that reliably controls motha (Cyperus rotundus, nutsedge), the hardest weed in sugarcane, while metribuzin takes care of broadleaf weeds and grasses.

Tizom is a selective, systemic, post-emergence herbicide: it is sprayed after the weeds have come up, and the cane is not harmed when it is used as the label directs. One spray covers narrow-leaf weeds, broadleaf weeds and nutsedge together, and the combination keeps the field clean for longer than either active alone.

Spray when the weeds are young and actively growing, with enough water for good cover. Tizom was launched first in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Follow the dose and timing on the Dhanuka label.

faqs.a: Halosulfuron methyl 6% plus metribuzin 50% WG.
Sugarcane.
Yes. Halosulfuron methyl in Tizom controls Cyperus rotundus (motha), along with broadleaf and grassy weeds.
Post-emergence, when the weeds are young and actively growing. Follow the timing and dose on the Dhanuka label.

hPfubvUUkHn4WIh1mYLb.description:
Sempra from Dhanuka contains halosulfuron methyl 75% WG, a selective herbicide made for one of the toughest weeds in Indian fields: motha, or nutsedge (Cyperus rotundus). Motha regrows from underground tubers, so cutting or hoeing only brings it back. Halosulfuron is absorbed by the leaves and moves down to the tubers, stopping the weed from regrowing.

Sempra is used in sugarcane and maize, where it is sprayed after the weeds have come up. It is a very concentrated granule, which is why the packs are small: 18 g and 36 g. Dissolve it fully in a little water before adding it to the tank, and add a surfactant only if the label asks for it.

Spray when motha is at the three to five leaf stage and actively growing; very dry weather slows the effect. Visible yellowing takes a week or more, and full control two to three weeks. Follow the dose and crop list on the Dhanuka label.

faqs.a: Mainly motha (nutsedge, Cyperus rotundus), including regrowth from its tubers.

faqs.q: In which crops can I use Sempra?
faqs.a: Sugarcane and maize, as listed on the label.

faqs.q: Why is the pack so small?
faqs.a: Halosulfuron methyl 75% WG is highly concentrated, so only a few grams are needed per acre. Follow the label dose.

faqs.q: How long does it take to work?
faqs.a: The weed stops growing quickly; yellowing shows in about a week and full control in two to three weeks.

crdWl9x2nxWByhoxoPf4.description:
Gluco Potash-X from SuvarnaBhumi is a liquid potassium nutrient containing 22% potassium gluconate. Gluconate is an organic carrier: it helps potassium enter the leaf quickly when sprayed and moves easily inside the plant. This makes it useful as a foliar spray at the stages when crops need extra potassium most, such as flowering, fruit filling and grain filling.

Potassium controls water use in the plant, builds sugar and starch in fruits and grains, and strengthens cell walls. Crops with enough potassium have better fruit size, colour, shine and keeping quality, and stand up better to drought and disease. It is used in vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops.

Gluco Potash is a fertilizer, not a pesticide. It can usually be sprayed with water-soluble fertilizers; test a small mix first before adding it to pesticide sprays. Follow the dose on the pack for your crop stage.

faqs.a: 22% potassium gluconate in liquid form, according to the listing.
From flowering through fruit or grain development, when the crop's need for potassium is highest.
No. It is a potassium fertilizer for foliar feeding. It does not control pests or diseases.
Vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops, especially where fruit size and quality matter.

9qg6pmBO8DsAJ92TnDfj.description:
Karate from Syngenta contains lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC, a synthetic pyrethroid insecticide. It acts on contact and through ingestion, attacking the insect's nervous system, which gives a fast knockdown of chewing and some sucking pests. Lambda-cyhalothrin also has a repellent effect, so treated plants are less attractive to pests for some days after spraying.

Karate is used against bollworms, caterpillars, leaf folders, stem borers, jassids and thrips in crops such as cotton, rice, chilli, tomato, brinjal and pulses, depending on the label. Because it acts on contact, coverage matters: spray both sides of the leaves, and spray at the first sign of the pest rather than after damage has spread.

Pyrethroids should be rotated with insecticides from other groups to avoid resistance. Karate is toxic to fish and bees, so keep it away from ponds and avoid spraying flowering crops when bees are active. Follow the dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Karate?
faqs.a: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC.
Chewing pests such as bollworms, caterpillars, stem borers and leaf folders, and some sucking pests such as jassids and thrips, in the crops on its label.

faqs.q: How often can I spray it?
faqs.a: Follow the number of sprays and waiting period on the label, and rotate with insecticides from other groups to prevent resistance.

faqs.q: Is Karate harmful to bees and fish?
faqs.a: Yes. Avoid spraying flowering crops while bees forage, and keep it away from ponds, canals and wells.

Hhf1qiBLdQgeC74Bndld.description:
Ridomil Gold from Syngenta is a fungicide for downy mildew, late blight and other diseases caused by oomycete pathogens (Phytophthora, Pythium, Peronospora and similar). The widely sold Ridomil Gold MZ combines metalaxyl-M, a systemic active that moves inside the plant and stops infection that has already started, with mancozeb, a contact active that protects the leaf surface against new infection.

It is used in potato and tomato against late blight, in grapes and cucurbits against downy mildew, and in other crops listed on the label. Apply it preventively when weather favours disease (cool nights, dew, cloudy humid days) or at the first symptoms. The systemic part gives a curative effect for a short time after infection; the contact part keeps protecting the leaf.

To keep metalaxyl-M effective, do not spray it again and again: use it two or three times a season at most, and alternate with fungicides from other groups. Follow the dose and crop list on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: Which diseases does Ridomil Gold control?
faqs.a: Diseases caused by oomycetes: late blight of potato and tomato, downy mildew of grapes and cucurbits, and others listed on the label.
Both. Metalaxyl-M is systemic and mancozeb is contact, so it protects the leaf and acts inside the plant.
Before or at the first sign of disease, especially in cool, humid weather. Follow the label for spray intervals.

faqs.q: Can I use it all season?
faqs.a: Limit it to two or three sprays a season and alternate with other fungicide groups so the disease does not become resistant.

iTx1bO0gnZHhKZ301Nnt.description:
Topas from Syngenta contains penconazole 10% EC, a systemic triazole fungicide best known for controlling powdery mildew. Penconazole is absorbed by the leaves and moves upward in the plant, protecting new growth as well as the sprayed surface. It stops the fungus building its cell membranes, which halts both new infection and the spread of patches already present.

Topas is widely used on grapes, and on vegetables and fruit crops such as chilli, mango, apple and cucurbits where powdery mildew is a problem, depending on the label. The white, powdery patches on leaves, shoots or fruit are the sign to act; early sprays at the first patches work far better than late ones.

Because it is concentrated, the dose per litre is small, so measure carefully. Rotate Topas with fungicides from other groups to avoid resistance, and follow the dose, spray interval and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Topas?
faqs.a: Penconazole 10% EC.
Mainly powdery mildew, in crops such as grapes, chilli, mango and cucurbits as listed on the label.
Yes. It is absorbed by the leaves and moves upward, protecting new growth.
Follow the dose and spray interval on the Syngenta label for your crop; measure carefully, as the rate per litre is small.

PRAA5LU6vXxyQbLd6TYy.description:
Kavach Flo from Syngenta is a contact fungicide based on chlorothalonil, in a flowable liquid formulation that mixes easily in the tank. Chlorothalonil forms a protective layer on the leaf and kills fungal spores as they germinate. It acts at many sites in the fungus at once, so resistance to it is very rare, which makes it a reliable partner to rotate with systemic fungicides.

Kavach Flo is used against leaf spots, early blight, anthracnose, fruit rots and similar diseases in crops such as potato, tomato, chilli, groundnut and fruit crops, as listed on the label. Being a contact fungicide, it protects only what it covers: spray before disease sets in or at the very first spots, and repeat at the interval on the label, especially after rain.

Note that Kavach Flo is a fungicide, not a fertilizer. Follow the dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label, and wear gloves and eye protection while mixing.

faqs.a: A chlorothalonil-based contact fungicide from Syngenta in a flowable formulation. It is not a fertilizer.
Leaf spots, early blight, anthracnose, fruit rots and other fungal diseases on the crops listed on its label.
Preventively, before disease appears or at the first spots, and again at the label interval, especially after rain.

faqs.q: Can I rotate it with systemic fungicides?
faqs.a: Yes. Chlorothalonil acts at many sites in the fungus, so it is a good rotation partner that helps prevent resistance.

6Mv6T9TVuBm3YVmS7J6O.description:
Nano Urea is IFFCO's liquid nitrogen fertilizer, made with nitrogen in nano-particle form. It is sprayed on the leaves instead of being spread on the soil. The tiny particles enter through the leaf pores and release nitrogen inside the plant, so much less nitrogen is lost to the air or washed out of the soil than with granular urea.

IFFCO recommends Nano Urea as a foliar spray at the stages when the crop needs nitrogen most: usually one spray at active tillering or branching, and a second before flowering. It is used in cereals such as wheat, rice and maize, in pulses, oilseeds, cotton, vegetables and fruit crops. Farmers use it to replace part of the top-dressed granular urea; the basal dose of nitrogen still goes into the soil.

Shake the bottle well, spray in the morning or evening when the leaf pores are open, and avoid spraying just before rain. A 500 ml bottle covers about one acre for one spray.

faqs.q: How do I use Nano Urea?
faqs.a: IFFCO recommends 2–4 ml per litre of water as a foliar spray, at active growth and again before flowering. Follow the instructions on the bottle.

faqs.q: Can Nano Urea fully replace granular urea?
faqs.a: No. It replaces part of the top-dressed urea. The basal nitrogen dose at sowing should still be applied to the soil.

faqs.q: How much area does one bottle cover?
faqs.a: One 500 ml bottle is meant for about one acre per spray.

faqs.q: When is the best time of day to spray?
faqs.a: Early morning or evening, when the leaf pores are open and the spray does not dry too fast. Avoid spraying if rain is expected within a few hours.

xMZfZAkpnXzV2m3WWrIH.description:
Kazoo is a plant nutrient containing ortho silicic acid (OSA) 2.0% WSL, the form of silicon that plants can absorb directly. Soil contains plenty of silicon, but mostly in forms roots cannot take up; ortho silicic acid is ready to use. Silicon builds up in the cell walls of leaves and stems, making them stronger and more upright.

Stronger tissue helps the crop in several ways: leaves stand better and catch more light, stems lodge less, the plant loses less water in dry spells, and the hard layer makes it harder for sucking pests and fungal spores to get in. Silicon also helps the plant handle heat and salt stress, and supports better uptake of other nutrients. Kazoo is used in fruits, vegetables, flowers and field crops such as rice, sugarcane and wheat.

It is applied as a foliar spray or through drip at the vegetative and flowering stages. Follow the dose on the pack for your crop.

faqs.a: Ortho silicic acid (OSA) 2.0% WSL, a plant-available form of silicon.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of silicon for crops?
faqs.a: Stronger leaves and stems, less lodging, better tolerance to drought, heat and salt stress, and a tougher barrier against sucking pests and fungal infection.
As a foliar spray or through drip irrigation, at the vegetative and flowering stages. Follow the dose on the pack.
Fruits, vegetables, flowers and field crops such as rice, sugarcane and wheat.

Khnn66dLVddRPT4TZ2TU.description:
Karan Veer is a liquid biostimulant from Hifield Organics containing 20% plant-source protein hydrolysate. Protein hydrolysates are proteins broken down into amino acids and short peptides. Plants absorb these quickly through leaves and roots and use them as building blocks, so the crop saves the energy it would spend making them itself.

The effect is strongest at demanding stages: flowering, fruit set and fruit development, and recovery after stress such as heat, cold, waterlogging or a heavy pesticide spray. Amino acids also help the plant take up and use other nutrients, which is why biostimulants like Karan Veer are often sprayed together with water-soluble fertilizers. It suits vegetables, fruit crops and field crops.

Karan Veer comes in 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre packs. Spray it on the leaves or apply through drip at the growth stages where you want the push, and follow the dose on the pack.

faqs.a: 20% protein hydrolysate from plant sources (amino acids and peptides).
Before and during flowering, at fruit set and fruit development, and to help the crop recover after stress.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with fertilizers?
faqs.a: It is commonly sprayed with water-soluble fertilizers. Test a small mix first before adding pesticides to the same tank.
As a foliar spray or through drip irrigation. Follow the dose on the pack.

5cg6cDoHI3B5yXTLCU8S.description:
Amaze XL is a plant growth stimulant made from seaweed extract and amino acids. Seaweed extracts carry natural plant growth substances and trace elements, while amino acids are ready-made building blocks the plant can use straight away. Together they support flowering, fruit setting, greener leaves and steady growth.

Farmers use Amaze XL at the stages where the crop needs a push: during vegetative growth, before and during flowering, and at fruit set, and after stress such as heat, cold or a heavy spray. Because it is a nutrition and growth product, it can be used alongside the normal fertilizer schedule; it does not replace NPK. It suits vegetables, fruit crops, flowers and field crops.

Amaze XL is available in 250 ml and 500 ml packs. Apply it as a foliar spray in the morning or evening, and follow the dose given on the pack for your crop.

faqs.q: What is Amaze XL made of?
faqs.a: Seaweed extract and amino acids.

faqs.q: What does it do for the crop?
faqs.a: It supports flowering, fruit setting, leaf greenness and growth, and helps the crop recover from stress.
No. It is a growth stimulant. It does not control pests or diseases.
During vegetative growth, before and during flowering, and at fruit set. Follow the dose on the pack.

ra5xPnPeXNZAelOZtEOF.description:
AS 712 is a hybrid maize (corn) seed bred for high yield and good grain quality. Hybrid maize gives uniform plants with strong vigour and well-filled, even cobs, which is what both grain buyers and poultry-feed traders look for. AS 712 is suited to both kharif and rabi seasons, which gives farmers flexibility in planning.

For the best results, sow in well-prepared, well-drained soil with good organic matter, at the spacing advised on the seed pack. Maize responds strongly to nitrogen and needs it at knee height and before tasselling, along with phosphorus and potassium at sowing. Keep the field free of weeds for the first 30 to 40 days, and watch for fall armyworm in the early whorl stage.

Hybrid seed should be bought fresh each season; seed saved from a hybrid crop does not give the same yield. Each 4 kg pack is treated and graded for good germination.

faqs.q: Which season is AS 712 suitable for?
faqs.a: Both kharif and rabi, according to the listing.

faqs.q: Can I save seed from my AS 712 crop to sow next season?
faqs.a: No. Seed from a hybrid crop does not give the same uniformity or yield. Buy fresh seed each season.

faqs.q: What is the main pest to watch for?
faqs.a: Fall armyworm in the early whorl stage. Check the whorls regularly from emergence and act early.
Maize needs nitrogen in splits (at sowing, knee height and before tasselling) plus phosphorus and potassium at sowing. Follow a soil test where possible.

alXNM9Y3wtuZqJib7BDd.description:
Amistar Top from Syngenta is a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide combining azoxystrobin 18.2% and difenoconazole 11.4% SC. Azoxystrobin stops the fungus from producing energy and has strong preventive action; difenoconazole stops it building its cell membranes and adds curative action against infections that have already started. Using two modes of action also lowers the risk of resistance.

Amistar Top controls blights, leaf spots, rusts, powdery mildew, sheath blight and similar diseases in crops such as rice, wheat, maize, cotton, tomato, chilli, onion, turmeric and sugarcane, as listed on the label. It is absorbed into the leaf and spreads within it, so it keeps working even after light rain once the spray has dried.

Spray at the first signs of disease, or preventively when the weather favours it. The seller's listing gives 200 ml per acre, subject to the crop-specific label. Use enough water for full coverage, and follow the spray interval and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

wpG71xA4yHShQmJMawTh.description:
Maze (Ojal) is listed by the seller as fodder maize seed, called charyachi maka in Marathi. It is meant for growing green fodder for dairy animals rather than for grain. The seller describes it as a tall-growing type that reaches about 10 to 12 feet. The listing does not name the seed company or a variety code, so check the bag and its tag for these details, along with the germination percentage and lot number, before sowing.

Dairy farmers grow fodder maize because it establishes quickly and gives leafy, juicy fodder that animals eat readily. For green fodder or silage it is usually cut around the milk to early dough stage of the cob, when both the quantity and the feeding value of the fodder are good. Cut too early, the fodder is watery; cut too late, the stems turn hard and less digestible.

For a good crop, sow in well-drained soil with enough farmyard manure, keep the field free of weeds during the first month, and irrigate regularly, as maize does not tolerate either drought or waterlogging well. Each pack holds 4 kg of seed. Follow the seed rate and spacing given on the bag.

faqs.q: What is this seed used for?

QlsamDYSLYKhFgnr64rj.description:
Clavengo is a non-selective herbicide containing glufosinate ammonium 13.5% SL. It kills almost any green weed it touches, grassy or broadleaf, by blocking an enzyme the plant needs to process ammonia. Ammonia builds up inside the leaf, and the weed dries out quickly, usually within a few days.

Glufosinate acts mainly on contact and moves only a little within the plant, so good coverage is important: spray all green parts of the weeds evenly. It is used to clear weeds before sowing, along field bunds, in orchards and plantations, and between rows of crops using a hood or shield so the spray does not touch the crop. Being non-selective, it will damage any crop leaves it lands on.

Clavengo comes in 500 ml and 1 litre packs. Spray on a calm day when the weeds are actively growing, and avoid spraying just before rain. Follow the dose and uses on the label.

faqs.a: Glufosinate ammonium 13.5% SL.

faqs.q: How is it different from glyphosate?
faqs.a: Glufosinate acts faster but mostly on contact, so it needs good coverage; glyphosate is slower but moves to the roots.

spxjewbVyEoGw9xBtMKM.description:
Amipro-K is a liquid phosphorus and potassium fertilizer made for quick uptake through the leaves or the drip line. It is fully soluble and free of sodium and chlorine, which matters for crops that are sensitive to salt, and it delivers nutrients in a form the plant can use straight away, so small doses go a long way.

Phosphorus supports root growth, flowering and energy transfer in the plant; potassium builds fruit size, sugar content, colour and keeping quality, and helps the plant manage water. A P and K feed like Amipro-K is used mainly from flowering through fruit development, and to support root growth after transplanting. It suits vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops.

Amipro-K is a fertilizer, not a pesticide, even though it may be filed with crop protection products in some lists. Apply it as a foliar spray or through drip, and follow the dose on the pack for your crop stage.

ogbzRDaOODZx65b4F65M.description:
Trust from NACL Industries contains emamectin benzoate 5% SG, an insecticide made for caterpillars. Emamectin benzoate is taken in by the larva when it feeds on treated leaves; within hours the caterpillar stops feeding and is paralysed, and it dies over the next two to four days. It also penetrates the leaf (translaminar action), so caterpillars feeding on the underside are reached too.

Trust is used against fruit borers, shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms and other caterpillar pests in crops such as chilli, tomato, brinjal, okra, cabbage, onion and maize, as listed on the label. It works best on young larvae, so spray when you first see eggs hatching or early feeding damage.

It is a soluble granule: dissolve it in a little water before adding it to the tank. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the NACL label, and rotate with insecticides from other groups.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Trust?

Caterpillar pests such as fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth and armyworms on the crops listed on its label.

faqs.q: Does it control sucking pests like whitefly?

1gFATYy3y81N4lf3y98U.description:
AS 771 is a hybrid maize seed produced and processed for high germination, genetic purity and field performance. The seed is cleaned and graded to remove inert matter and weed seeds, and the listing gives a germination rate of 90%. Uniform seed gives an even stand, which is the base for even cobs and a good harvest.

Sow AS 771 in well-drained, well-prepared soil at the spacing on the seed pack. Maize needs nitrogen in splits (at sowing, at knee height and before tasselling) with phosphorus and potassium at sowing, and enough water at tasselling and silking, when stress hurts yield most. Keep the field weed-free for the first five to six weeks.

Scout the young crop for fall armyworm in the whorls and act early if you see feeding holes. Hybrid seed should be bought fresh each season. Each pack holds 4 kg.

faqs.a: Check the whorls of young plants regularly from emergence and spray at the first sign of feeding, following a registered product's label.

QTrGz1Xz6xsYvRv7q9i4.description:
NPK 11:11:8 from R. M. Phosphates & Chemicals (RMPCL) is a water-soluble suspension fertilizer with balanced nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, fortified with micronutrients. The liquid suspension format lets the nutrients reach the plant quickly through a foliar spray, and the added micronutrients help correct hidden deficiencies that hold back growth even when NPK is enough.

With nitrogen and phosphorus in equal parts and a little less potassium, the 11:11:8 grade suits the early and middle stages of the crop: vegetative growth, root building and branching. It is used in vegetables, field crops and fruit crops as a supplement to soil-applied fertilizer, especially when the crop needs a quick push or the soil is dry and roots cannot take up nutrients well.

Shake the bottle well before use, spray in the morning or evening, and follow the dose given on the pack. Test a small mix first if you want to combine it with pesticides.

Rosentra from Syngenta India contains topramezone 336 g/L (w/v) SC, a selective post-emergence herbicide for maize. Topramezone belongs to the triketone group of HPPD inhibitors: it blocks an enzyme the weed needs to make protective pigments, so new leaves turn white (bleach) in sunlight and the weed dies within one to two weeks. Maize breaks down topramezone quickly, which is why the crop is not harmed.

Rosentra controls both grassy and broadleaf weeds in maize, including crowfoot grass, crabgrass, Eleusine and many broadleaf weeds, when sprayed at the early post-emergence stage, typically when weeds have two to four leaves. It is very concentrated, which is why it comes in small 15 ml, 30 ml and 75 ml packs. HPPD herbicides of this type are usually sprayed with an adjuvant to improve uptake.

Confidor Super from Bayer contains imidacloprid 30.5% SC, a systemic neonicotinoid insecticide (IRAC group 4A). The plant absorbs it and carries it to the leaves, so sucking pests that feed on the sap are controlled even on parts the spray did not reach directly. The SC formulation spreads well on the leaf and is absorbed quickly.

Confidor Super is used against aphids, jassids, thrips, whiteflies, brown planthopper and white-backed planthopper in crops such as cotton, paddy and chilli, as listed on the label. The seller's listing gives 60–75 ml per hectare for cotton and paddy; for chilli, follow the current label.

Delegate from Corteva Agriscience contains spinetoram 11.7% SC, an insecticide from the spinosyn group (IRAC group 5). Delegate controls thrips and caterpillar pests such as fruit borers, diamondback moth and leaf miners in the crops listed on its label, including chilli, onion, brinjal, cabbage and grapes. The Karan Arjun Onion Tannashak Kit is a ready-made weed control and crop support programme for half an acre of onion. This is a sticker, also called a sticking agent: an adjuvant that is added to the spray tank along with a pesticide or a foliar nutrient. The listing does not name the maker or the ingredients, so this page explains what a sticker does in general. Read the label on the bottle for its exact composition and dose.

When a spray dries on a leaf, rain, dew or irrigation water can wash much of it off within hours. A sticker helps the spray deposit hold onto the leaf surface, so more of the product stays where it is needed and less is wasted. Many stickers also help droplets spread out instead of beading up, which matters on waxy, smooth leaves such as onion, garlic, cabbage and chilli. A sticker is not a pesticide or a fertilizer and does nothing on its own; it only helps the main product work better.

Use it in sprays where coverage and staying power matter, especially in the rainy season or when dew is heavy. Fill the tank with water, mix the pesticide or nutrient first, and add the sticker last. Use only the small quantity given on the label; adding more than the label rate gives no extra benefit. The listing offers 50 ml and 100 ml bottles.

5c34OUjfWHWqGVoEew59.description:
Amistar from Syngenta contains azoxystrobin 23% SC, a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide from the strobilurin group. Azoxystrobin stops fungal spores from germinating and blocks the fungus's energy supply. It moves into the leaf and spreads across it, so it protects areas next to where the drop landed, and it has a mild greening effect that helps the crop stay healthy longer.

Amistar controls powdery mildew, downy mildew, anthracnose, blight and similar diseases in the crops on its label, including grapes, chilli, tomato, potato, rice and others. It works best as a preventive spray, or at the first signs of disease, because strobilurins stop infection before it takes hold.

To keep azoxystrobin effective, do not use it in back-to-back sprays: alternate it with fungicides from other groups and follow the maximum number of sprays on the label. Use the dose and spray interval on the Syngenta label for your crop.

Calaris Xtra from Syngenta is a selective, systemic post-emergence herbicide for maize and sugarcane, containing mesotrione 2.27% w/w and atrazine 22.7% w/w SC. MW6IWE2XPJhAhlleS806.description:
Karan Arjun Root Booster is a biostimulant from Karan Arjun, made to help crops build a strong, healthy root system. The seller describes it as supporting root development and overall plant vigour, improving soil fertility and structure, and helping the crop take up nutrients, so that young plants establish well after sowing or transplanting.

Roots do most of their growing in the first weeks of a crop, and a weak start often shows up later as uneven plants and a poor response to fertilizer. A root booster is used at this stage, and again when the crop is under stress, to encourage new roots and better use of the nutrients already in the soil. It does not replace fertilizer; it works alongside a normal fertilizer programme. Karan Arjun also includes Root Booster in the first spray of its Onion Tannashak Kit, where it is meant to support the onion crop's growth alongside the weed-control spray.

Common uses are in vegetables after transplanting, in field crops during vegetative growth, and in fruit crops after pruning, when new growth starts. Vibrance Integral from Syngenta is a seed treatment that protects seed and seedlings from both fungal diseases and insect pests. A dispersant keeps the particles separated so they dissolve quickly and evenly.

The listing gives 50 ml per 200 litres of water, for both drip irrigation and foliar spray. Add JEFHA MAX PRO to the water first, then add the fertilizer and stir. Folio Gold from Syngenta is a broad-spectrum fungicide in suspension concentrate (SC) form that combines systemic and contact action. It is widely used against downy mildew and blight. Ci3MMwL7O2Z2sohvnUOp.description:
Amistar Top from Syngenta is a systemic fungicide that combines two actives in one suspension concentrate (SC): azoxystrobin 18.2% w/w and difenoconazole 11.4% w/w. Azoxystrobin is a strobilurin that cuts off the energy supply of the fungus and protects the leaf before infection takes hold. Difenoconazole is a triazole that stops the fungus from building its cell membranes and works on infections that have already started. Because the two act in different ways, the mix gives both preventive and curative action and lowers the chance of the fungus becoming resistant.

In India this combination is registered on a long list of crops, including chilli (anthracnose and powdery mildew), tomato (early and late blight), paddy (blast and sheath blight), maize, wheat (rust and powdery mildew), cotton, onion (purple blotch, Stemphylium blight and downy mildew), turmeric, sugarcane, groundnut, black gram and soybean. Check the label for the diseases approved on your crop.

The seller's listing gives 200 ml per acre, citing Syngenta's product overview, and advises using the crop-specific dose, spray volume and schedule on the registered label. Spray at the first signs of disease, or earlier when the weather favours it, with full cover of the plant. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Amistar Top per acre?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives 200 ml per acre, based on Syngenta's product overview. Use the crop-specific dose and water volume printed on the label, since they can differ by crop.

faqs.q: Which diseases does Amistar Top control?
faqs.a: Blights, leaf spots, powdery mildew, rust, anthracnose, blast, sheath blight, purple blotch and similar fungal diseases on the crops named on its label, such as chilli, tomato, paddy, wheat, onion and turmeric.

faqs.q: Does it work after the disease has appeared?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. Difenoconazole acts on early infections, while azoxystrobin protects healthy tissue. It works best when sprayed at the first symptoms rather than after the disease has spread.

faqs.q: Can I spray it again and again?
faqs.a: Do not go beyond the number of sprays on the label, and rotate it with fungicides from other groups so the fungus does not become resistant to either active.

FASTER from UNIMAX is an organic silicon-based adjuvant: a wetting, spreading, penetrating and dispersing agent added to pesticide and fertilizer sprays. Better coverage and penetration mean the pesticide or fertilizer in the tank works better, often at the same dose. The water-dispersible granules mix easily without dust; pour them into a partly filled tank while stirring. Cabrio Top comes in a 600 g pack. Follow the BASF label for the dose and waiting period on your crop.

h4I0A77HaUpnpFkoIbGX.description:
Crystal Gramoxone contains paraquat dichloride 24% SL, a fast-acting, non-selective contact herbicide. It kills the green parts of any plant it touches by disrupting photosynthesis; weeds start to wilt within hours in sunlight and dry out in a day or two. It does not move into the roots, so it burns down the top growth of weeds rather than killing deep-rooted perennials.

Paraquat is used to clear annual grasses and broadleaf weeds before sowing, between crop rows with a shield, on bunds and in plantations, only where the registered label allows. It becomes inactive on contact with soil, so it leaves no soil residue for the next crop.

Paraquat is highly toxic to people if swallowed, and there is no antidote. Never store it in drink bottles, keep it locked away from children, wear gloves, a mask and eye protection while mixing and spraying, and do not spray in windy weather. Follow the dose and uses on the registered label.

faqs.a: Paraquat dichloride 24% SL.

SWAL CANORA EZ contains clethodim 13% w/w EC, a selective post-emergence herbicide for grassy weeds in cotton, soybean and onion. Spray when the grasses are young and actively growing.

Canora EZ does not control broadleaf weeds or sedges, so plan a separate herbicide for those if needed. Spray on a calm day, avoid rain soon after spraying, and follow the registered label for the dose and water volume.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use it on?

unb6QweynV1zQTNLtGXB.description:
ARJUN ASTRA-54 is a 100% water-soluble potash (potassium) fertilizer. Potassium is the nutrient of fruit and grain quality: it moves sugars into fruits and grains, builds fruit size, colour and shine, strengthens cell walls and helps the plant manage water. Crops with enough potassium also handle disease and dry spells better.

The listing gives the dose as 2–3 ml per litre of water for foliar spray and 2–4 ml per litre for drip irrigation, and lists vegetable crops such as tomato, chilli, brinjal, bitter gourd and okra, and fruit crops such as apple, grapes and mango. Use it mainly from flowering onward, through fruit setting and fruit development.

ARJUN ASTRA-54 comes in 500 g, 1 kg and 2 kg packs. Spray in the morning or evening, and test a small mix first before combining it with pesticides in one tank.

md9W0uhPPUwOZzvJO2E6.description:
Curzate M8 from Corteva Agriscience is a fungicide that combines cymoxanil 8% and mancozeb 64% in a wettable powder (WP). The two actives work in different ways. Cymoxanil is taken into the leaf and acts inside the plant tissue, so it can check an infection in its early stage, before spots become visible. Mancozeb stays on the leaf surface as a protective layer and attacks fungal spores at many sites at once, which also slows the build-up of resistance.

Curzate is used mainly against late blight in potato and tomato and downy mildew in grapes and cucumber; the seller's listing also mentions gummosis in citrus. These diseases spread quickly in cool, humid or rainy weather, so the spray works best when applied early: just before the disease is expected or at the very first symptoms. Make a paste of the powder in a little water, add it to the tank, and spray so that both sides of the leaves are covered.

The seller's listing gives 1.5 kg per hectare in about 500 litres of water. Check the Indian pack label for your crop's exact rate, spray interval and waiting period before harvest. This listing is a 1.2 kg pack. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: Cymoxanil 8% plus mancozeb 64% in a wettable powder (WP).

cUE4pDRsrkaTeVeFm4St.description:
Slayer Pro is a seed-treatment insecticide containing thiamethoxam 30% FS (a flowable suspension made for treating seed), sold under the GSP Crop Science brand. Thiamethoxam is a neonicotinoid. When it is coated on the seed, the germinating seedling takes it up through its roots and carries it into the young stem and leaves, so the plant is protected from inside during its most delicate first weeks.

This early protection is aimed at insects that attack seedlings, mainly sucking pests such as aphids, jassids and thrips, and some soil insects, as listed on the label. The seller mentions crops such as cotton, maize, wheat and soybean. Treating the seed puts far less chemical into the field than an early spray, and it helps the crop come up as an even, healthy stand.

Mix the measured quantity with a little water to make a slurry, coat the seed evenly in a drum or bag, dry it in the shade and sow it soon after. Treated seed must never be eaten or fed to animals; mark the bags and keep them away from food and grain. Use the dose per kg of seed given on the label for your crop. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask while treating seed, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: Thiamethoxam 30% FS, a seed-treatment formulation.

faqs.q: Do I spray Slayer Pro on the crop?
faqs.a: No. It is meant for coating seed before sowing. The seedling takes up the insecticide as it germinates.

faqs.q: How much should I use per kg of seed?
faqs.a: It depends on the crop. Follow the dose on the label for the crop you are sowing.

faqs.q: Can I store treated seed or feed leftover seed to animals?
faqs.a: Sow treated seed soon after treatment. Never eat it or feed it to animals, and keep treated bags clearly marked and away from food and grain.

HLiU8JMTvyMal3C8krSP.description:
Biozyme Crop+ from Biostadt India is a liquid biostimulant based on seaweed extract. It is not a replacement for NPK fertilizer. It works alongside your normal fertilizer programme, helping the crop grow actively, build roots and make better use of the nutrients already applied. The seller's listing also describes support for flowering and fruit set, less flower and fruit drop, and better tolerance of stresses such as heat, dry spells and transplanting shock.

Biostadt lists Crop+ for all crops, with better vegetative growth as its main aim. The seller's listing names field crops such as cotton, paddy, wheat, maize, sugarcane, soybean and groundnut; vegetables such as tomato, chilli, brinjal, onion and potato; fruit crops such as grapes, banana, mango, pomegranate and citrus; and flowers.

It is applied as a foliar spray. Biostadt gives a dose of 250 to 300 ml per acre, and the seller's listing gives 1 to 2 ml per litre of water, with the advice to follow crop-specific label recommendations. Useful timings are the vegetative stage, just before flowering, at flowering and during fruit development. Spray in the morning or evening, and mix a small test batch first if you plan to add it to a pesticide spray.

faqs.q: How much Biozyme Crop+ should I use?
faqs.a: Biostadt gives 250 to 300 ml per acre. The seller's listing gives 1 to 2 ml per litre of water. Follow the label for your crop.

sCSQDtTo4wQayzxeBeA6.description:
Baleco 11:11:8 is a liquid NPK fertilizer for foliar spraying. The grade means it carries nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in the ratio 11:11:8, and the seller's listing says it is fortified with zinc (0.7%) and boron (0.5 to 0.7%). The seller describes it as a nano-technology based product. The listing does not name the manufacturer, so check the bottle for the maker's name and the grade printed on the label.

A balanced NPK spray with zinc and boron is useful during active growth and around flowering, when the crop's demand is high and the roots alone may not keep up. Zinc supports leaf growth and enzyme activity, and boron is needed for flowering, pollen and fruit set, so a shortage of either can lead to flower drop or poorly formed fruit. The listing names a wide range of crops: cotton, paddy, wheat, maize, sugarcane, tomato, chilli, onion, potato, grapes, pomegranate, banana, mango, citrus, other vegetables and fruit crops, and flowers.

The seller's listing gives 250 to 500 ml per acre, or 2 to 3 ml per litre of water, as a foliar spray during active vegetative growth, before flowering and during fruit development. A foliar spray adds to soil fertilizer; it does not replace the basal dose. Spray in the cool part of the day, and do a small jar test before mixing it with pesticides.

iBnBaDjm4KNTGfSz8yHV.description:
Evenso from Syngenta India is a selective herbicide containing oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC. Oxyfluorfen belongs to the diphenyl ether group and blocks an enzyme called PPO (protoporphyrinogen oxidase) in the weed. When sunlight falls on the treated weed, its cell membranes break down and young seedlings dry out and die. Sprayed on moist soil, it also forms a treated layer at the surface that kills weed seedlings as they come up, giving residual control for some time.

Evenso is used mainly as a pre-emergence spray, and as an early post-emergence spray only where the label allows it. It controls annual broadleaf weeds such as Chenopodium album (bathua) and Amaranthus viridis (chaulai), and certain annual grasses. The seller lists onion, direct-seeded rice, tea, potato, groundnut and mentha as crops; check that your crop is on the current Syngenta label before use.

Spray evenly with a flat-fan nozzle on moist soil, and avoid disturbing the soil surface afterwards, since that breaks the treated layer. The dose depends on the crop, so use the rate and water volume printed on the label. It comes in 100 ml, 250 ml and 500 ml packs. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: A selective herbicide from Syngenta India containing oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC.
Annual broadleaf weeds such as bathua (Chenopodium) and chaulai (Amaranthus), and certain annual grasses. It is much weaker on established perennial weeds.

lWcIPz7o857cL5WiZSfs.description:
Profex Super from NACL Industries (Nagarjuna) is a ready-mixed insecticide containing profenofos 40% and cypermethrin 4% in an emulsifiable concentrate (EC). The two actives come from different chemical groups. Profenofos is an organophosphate that blocks the acetylcholinesterase enzyme in the insect's nerves, while cypermethrin is a synthetic pyrethroid that acts on the sodium channels of nerve cells. Together they give contact and stomach action, a quick knockdown and some residual protection.

NACL lists Profex Super for the bollworm complex in cotton, the group of caterpillars that bore into squares and bolls, and also describes it as active on sucking and chewing pests. Spray when the pest is first seen and the larvae are still young, because older larvae inside the bolls are hard to reach. Cover the plant well, including squares, flowers and young bolls.

NACL's product page and the seller's listing both give 400 to 600 ml per acre for cotton. Follow the label for the water volume and the waiting period before picking, and do not repeat the same mixture spray after spray; alternate with insecticides from other groups. Abacin from Crystal Crop Protection is an insecticide and miticide containing abamectin 1.9% EC (emulsifiable concentrate). Abamectin is produced from a soil microorganism and acts on the nervous system of mites and insects, which are paralysed, stop feeding and die over the next few days. It works by contact and as a stomach poison, and it moves into the leaf (translaminar action), so it also reaches mites feeding on the underside of leaves, where spider mites usually live.

Crystal lists Abacin for control of the two-spotted spider mite (red spider mite) in roses. These tiny mites suck sap from the leaves, which become speckled, pale and bronzed, often with fine webbing. Heavy attacks cause leaf drop and poor flower quality, especially in hot, dry weather and in polyhouses.

Crystal gives a dose of 150 ml per acre for roses. Spray when mites first appear, cover both sides of the leaves well, and rotate with miticides from other chemical groups so that the mites do not become resistant. Use it only on the crops named on the label. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. Abamectin is very toxic to fish, so never wash the sprayer in ponds or canals.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Abacin for roses?
faqs.a: Crystal Crop Protection gives 150 ml per acre for two-spotted spider mite on roses. Use the water volume given on the label so both leaf surfaces are well covered.

Mites stop feeding soon after contact with the spray or the treated leaf, and most die over the next few days. Check the plants a few days after spraying to see whether a repeat spray is needed, as the label allows.

Onion Parth is a pink onion seed variety. According to the seller's listing, it can be grown in both kharif and rabi seasons and produces glossy pink bulbs of uniform shape and size. The Karan Arjun Onion Tannashak Kit (2 acre) is a ready weed-management programme for two acres of onion. It packs the products for two sprays into one kit, with the order of use written down, so the farmer does not have to buy several products separately and work out the combination.

XJuCdY6n9S1U0uthUmJG.description:
Isabion from Syngenta is a biostimulant made from amino acids and peptides, the building blocks of proteins. faqs.q: What is the dose of Isabion?

Farmers use Bahaar to support healthy vegetative growth, better flowering and fruit setting, and less flower and fruit drop. Glyclean Power is a non-selective herbicide containing glufosinate ammonium 13.5% w/w SL (soluble liquid), registered in India with the Central Insecticides Board. Despite the name, it is not a glyphosate product. Glufosinate blocks the glutamine synthetase enzyme in green plant tissue; ammonia then builds up inside the leaves and the weed burns down within a few days. It moves only a little inside the plant and acts mainly where the spray lands, so good coverage of the weed foliage matters.

The brand's product information lists it for tea and non-cropped areas. In tea it is listed against weeds such as Imperata cylindrica, Panicum repens, Borreria hispida, Digitaria, Commelina benghalensis, Ageratum conyzoides, Eleusine indica and Paspalum conjugatum. In non-crop areas it is listed against Echinochloa, Cynodon dactylon (doob grass), Cyperus rotundus (motha), Digitaria and Dactyloctenium.

Spray after the weeds have emerged, while they are young, green and actively growing, on a dry day with no rain due. It kills any green plant tissue it touches, so keep it away from crop leaves and green stems. The brand advises not mixing it with other chemicals. Follow the dose on the label. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. The pack size here is 1 litre.

uaRe0HQKIHHgdXD2VidC.description:
Touchdown from Syngenta is a non-selective, systemic herbicide containing glyphosate 41% SL (soluble liquid, as the isopropylamine salt). It is sprayed on weeds that have already come up. The green leaves absorb it and carry it down to the roots, rhizomes and other underground parts, where it blocks an enzyme (EPSP synthase) that plants need to make certain amino acids. Weeds stop growing, then turn yellow and dry over the following one to three weeks; perennial weeds with deep roots take the longest.

Because it kills almost any green plant it reaches, glyphosate 41% SL is registered in India for weed control in tea plantations and in non-cropped areas such as bunds, field borders, roadsides and fallow land. It controls annual and perennial grasses and broadleaf weeds, including hard-to-kill grasses such as doob grass (Cynodon dactylon) and Imperata.

Spray actively growing weeds that have plenty of green leaf, on a calm day, and keep the spray off crops and any plants you want to keep. Do not cut or plough the weeds for several days after spraying, so the chemical has time to move to the roots, and avoid spraying when rain is expected. Use the dose on the label. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food, animal feed and water sources.

faqs.q: Can I spray Touchdown in a standing crop?
faqs.a: No. It kills any green plant it touches. It is meant for tea plantations and non-cropped areas, and the spray must be kept away from crops.

faqs.q: How long does it take to kill weeds?
faqs.a: Weeds stop growing within a few days and dry out over one to three weeks. Deep-rooted perennial weeds take the longest and may need a repeat spray on regrowth.

faqs.q: Does it stop new weeds from coming up?
faqs.a: No. Glyphosate works only through green leaves and has no lasting effect in the soil, so weeds that germinate later will need another treatment.
Use the dose and water volume on the Syngenta label, which depend on the type of weeds and how dense they are.

MmMjrBOzh0Qkm163kA7q.description:
Power Gel is a humic-based plant nutrient sold as a gel in a 500 g pack. The seller's listing describes it as a combination of humates and fulvates, the active parts of humus, the dark organic matter found in fertile soil. The brand's product information gives the humate and fulvate content as 22%.

Humic substances are not fertilizers in the usual sense; they work by improving the soil around the roots. Humates help the soil hold water and nutrients and feed soil microbes, while fulvates, being much smaller molecules, help carry nutrients into the plant. The results farmers look for are more white roots, better early establishment and better use of the fertilizer already applied. They are most useful in soils that are low in organic matter.

The gel is dissolved in water before use, and the brand's information says it can be given through drip or drenching or as a foliar spray, at any crop stage. Follow the rate and number of applications printed on the pack. Use Power Gel along with normal fertilizers, not in place of them.

faqs.a: Humates and fulvates (humic and fulvic substances). The brand's information gives their content as 22%.

adBUdMfk0WDb3YL7KZY2.description:
Ulala from UPL is an insecticide containing flonicamid 50% WG (water-dispersible granules). Flonicamid works differently from most insecticides: sucking insects that feed on treated plants stop feeding within a short time, then starve and die over the next few days. It is systemic and translaminar, so it moves into the leaf and reaches pests feeding on the underside. UPL positions it mainly for sucking pest management in cotton, with long-lasting control and a good fit in IPM programmes.

The seller's listing names aphids, jassids, thrips and whiteflies in cotton, and planthoppers in rice. Because the insects stop feeding quickly, crop damage stops early even though dead insects may only be seen after two or three days. Flonicamid has its own mode-of-action group, so it is useful in rotation where pests no longer respond well to neonicotinoids or other common insecticides.

The seller's listing gives 150 g per hectare in 500 litres of water (about 60 g per acre in 200 litres) and a re-entry period of 24 hours, with crop-specific directions on the label. Disperse the granules in a little water before adding them to the tank, and spray for full coverage. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. Packs: 30 g and 60 g.

faqs.a: Flonicamid 50% WG.
Sucking pests: aphids, jassids, thrips and whiteflies in cotton, and planthoppers in rice, as named in the seller's listing.

faqs.q: Why do I still see insects a day after spraying?
faqs.a: Flonicamid stops feeding quickly, but the insects die over two to three days. Damage stops early even if insects are still visible.
The seller's listing gives 150 g per hectare in 500 litres of water, about 60 g per acre. Follow the crop-specific directions on the label.

Xbom4Zn5L3Ugk4N5pxw9.description:
Missile from Crystal Crop Protection is an insecticide containing emamectin benzoate 5% SG, a soluble granule from the avermectin group. It kills caterpillars by contact and as a stomach poison. Crystal describes translaminar action, which carries the active into the leaf so that larvae feeding on the underside are also controlled, feeding that stops roughly two hours after spraying, and rain-fastness of about four hours.

Missile is meant mainly for caterpillar pests. Crystal lists crops including cotton (bollworms), okra and brinjal (fruit and shoot borer), cabbage (diamondback moth), chilli (fruit borer, thrips and mites), red gram and chickpea (pod borer), grapes (thrips) and tea (tea looper). These match the uses registered in India for emamectin benzoate 5% SG.

The 100 g pack suits small fields. Dissolve the granules in a little water first, then add to the tank and spray when young larvae are seen, covering the whole plant. Use the dose and water volume printed on the label for your crop, and rotate with insecticides from different groups to slow resistance. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Missile?
faqs.a: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG (soluble granules), from the avermectin group.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use Missile on?
faqs.a: Crystal lists cotton, okra, brinjal, cabbage, chilli, red gram, chickpea, grapes and tea. Use it only on the crops named on the label.
Follow the crop-specific dose and water volume printed on the Missile label.

faqs.q: Is Missile the same as other emamectin benzoate 5% SG brands?
faqs.a: The active and strength are the same, but each brand has its own label. Follow the dose and crop list on the pack you buy.

HupZwgkDvFH9JE70l5zL.description:
Mega Sweet (ADV 6681) is a hybrid sweet sorghum from Advanta Seeds, grown as a fodder crop for dairy and livestock farmers. Advanta lists Mega Sweet among its forage varieties in India. The seller's listing describes tall plants with sweet, juicy stems, broad leaves and high biomass, suited to both green fodder and silage, and gives about 85 to 90 days to flowering or maturity.

According to the listing, it can be sown in spring and kharif, and also in rabi in southern India and Maharashtra, at a seed rate of 6 kg per acre. Sow in well-prepared, well-drained soil, give nitrogen in splits, and keep the field weed-free in the early weeks. The sugar in sweet stems makes the fodder palatable and helps silage ferment well.

One safety point applies to all sorghum fodder: young plants, fresh regrowth and drought-stressed crops can contain prussic acid (HCN), which is poisonous to cattle. Do not feed very young or stressed crop, and harvest at the stage recommended on the seed pack. Wilting the fodder or making silage lowers the risk. As a hybrid, fresh seed should be bought every season.

faqs.q: What is Mega Sweet used for?
faqs.a: Green fodder and silage for dairy animals and other livestock.

faqs.q: When is it ready to harvest?
faqs.a: The listing gives about 85 to 90 days to flowering or maturity. Harvest at the stage recommended on the seed pack for fodder or silage.

faqs.q: What seed rate should I use?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives 6 kg per acre.

faqs.q: Is sorghum fodder safe for cattle?
faqs.a: Yes, once the crop is mature enough. Young plants, regrowth and drought-stressed sorghum can contain prussic acid (HCN), which is poisonous. Do not feed very young or stressed crop; wilting or ensiling lowers the risk.

sources: ICAR Indian Farming article on sorghum fodder

amegLK9nSGDkQ4nTIUq2.description:
Oxykill from Dhanuka Agritech is a selective herbicide containing oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC, from the diphenyl ether group. Dhanuka describes it as both a pre-emergence and a post-emergence herbicide. It interferes with chlorophyll production in the weed, so that in sunlight the cell membranes are damaged and the seedlings dry up. On moist soil it also leaves a treated surface layer that kills weeds as they germinate.

Oxykill controls annual broadleaf weeds and some grasses, and suppresses some perennial weeds. Dhanuka's label covers direct-sown rice (against Echinochloa, Cyperus iria and Eclipta alba), tea (against Digitaria, Imperata, Paspalum and Borreria), onion (against Chenopodium album and Amaranthus viridis) and mentha (against a long list of grass and broadleaf weeds).

Dhanuka's product page gives these doses per acre: direct-sown rice, 260 to 400 ml in 200 litres of water as a pre-emergence spray; tea, 260 to 400 ml in 200 to 300 litres; onion, 170 to 340 ml in 200 to 300 litres; mentha, 362 ml in 200 litres. Spray evenly with a flat-fan nozzle and avoid disturbing the soil afterwards. This listing is a 250 ml pack. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Oxykill for onion?
faqs.a: Dhanuka's product page gives 170 to 340 ml per acre in 200 to 300 litres of water for onion.

faqs.q: Which crops is Oxykill used in?
faqs.a: Dhanuka lists direct-sown rice, tea, onion and mentha.

faqs.q: Is it a pre-emergence or post-emergence herbicide?
faqs.a: Dhanuka describes it as both. In direct-sown rice it is used pre-emergence. Follow the label timing for each crop.

faqs.q: Which weeds does it control in onion?
faqs.a: Dhanuka's label lists Chenopodium album (bathua) and Amaranthus viridis (chaulai) for onion.

faqs.q: Is Oxykill the same as Evenso?
faqs.a: Both contain oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC, but they are sold by different companies (Dhanuka and Syngenta). Follow the label of the product you buy.

OvD8l7aF2Cwv3l353SIa.description:
Glyphos 41 is a herbicide containing glyphosate 41% SL (soluble liquid), as stated on its label; the listing does not name the manufacturer. Glyphosate is a systemic, non-selective herbicide. Weeds turn yellow over several days and die within about one to two weeks, including perennial grasses such as doob (Cynodon) and Imperata, and sedges such as motha (Cyperus rotundus) that regrow after cutting.

In India, glyphosate 41% SL is registered for use in tea and in non-cropped areas such as bunds, field borders, channels and fallow land. It kills almost any green plant, so it must never be sprayed on a standing crop, and drift onto nearby crops must be avoided.

Spray when the weeds are actively growing and have plenty of leaf, using clean water, as muddy water weakens glyphosate. Do not spray if rain is expected within a few hours, and do not cut or plough the weeds for about a week after spraying, so the chemical can reach the roots. Follow the dose on the label. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. The pack size is 1 litre.

faqs.a: Yellowing starts in several days and weeds usually die in one to two weeks. Tough perennial weeds may need a second spray when they regrow.

faqs.q: Does it stop new weeds from coming up later?
faqs.a: No. Glyphosate has little activity in the soil, so it kills the weeds it is sprayed on but does not prevent new ones from germinating.

HCywhluMboykpbune8Le.description:
Vayego from Bayer is an insecticide containing tetraniliprole 18.18% SC (suspension concentrate). Tetraniliprole belongs to the diamide group, which acts on the muscles of insects. Soon after a pest feeds on a treated plant or is hit by the spray, its muscles stop working normally, it stops feeding and it dies. The active is taken up into the plant, and its effect lasts a long time, which can reduce the number of spray rounds needed in a season.

In India, Vayego is registered for two crops: rice, against yellow stem borer and leaf folder, and soybean, against girdle beetle, Spodoptera caterpillars and semilooper. It is aimed at chewing pests and is not labelled for sucking pests such as aphids, jassids or whitefly.

Spray at the early stage of attack, such as the first dead hearts or folded leaves in rice, or the first girdle beetle damage and young caterpillars in soybean, with full cover of the crop. Use the dose, water volume and waiting period printed on the Bayer label, and avoid spraying diamide insecticides back to back; rotate with other groups. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: Rice, against yellow stem borer and leaf folder, and soybean, against girdle beetle, Spodoptera and semilooper.
Use the dose and water volume printed on the Bayer label for your crop. Check the label each season, as recommendations can change.

faqs.q: When should I spray it in rice?
faqs.a: At the early stage of stem borer or leaf folder attack, when the first dead hearts or folded leaves appear, or as your local agriculture office advises.

faqs.q: Can I use Vayego on vegetables?
faqs.a: Only on crops named on the label. In India it is registered for rice and soybean.

02IWEm6LLMuSpycZ7F9R.description:
C-7 is a plant adjuvant: a product added to the spray tank to help the main spray work better. The seller's listing says it improves the spreading, sticking and penetration of foliar sprays by lowering the surface tension of the droplets, so they flatten out and wet the leaf instead of rolling off. It also says C-7 helps stop spray deposits from crystallizing on the leaf surface, so more of the applied product stays available to the plant.

It is meant to be used with compatible pesticides, fungicides or foliar fertilizers, and it is not a replacement for any of them. Adjuvants of this kind are most useful on waxy or hairy leaves, such as onion and cabbage, where a plain spray solution does not spread well.

The listing does not give a verified dose. Add C-7 at the rate printed on the pack, mix thoroughly, and follow the directions of the main product you are spraying. Do a small jar test before mixing it with a new product, and avoid spraying in strong wind or just before rain. The listing does not name the manufacturer, so check the label for the maker and the full directions.

faqs.a: According to the listing, it helps sprays spread, stick and penetrate on leaves and stops spray deposits from crystallizing.

faqs.q: How much C-7 should I add?
faqs.a: The listing does not give a verified dose. Use the rate printed on the pack.

faqs.q: Can I use C-7 on its own?
faqs.a: No. It has no pest-control or nutrient action of its own; it only improves the spray it is mixed with.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with any pesticide?
faqs.a: Check the labels of both products and do a small jar test first. If the mix curdles, separates or forms lumps, do not use it.

Eagle ECS is a silicon-based plant nutrient sold as a 500 g powder. The seller's listing gives its content as silica (SiO2) at 85% with organic excipients, and describes it as a functional plant nutrient for foliar spraying. The maker's name is not given in the listing.

This makes the tissue tougher, which can help the plant cope better with sucking pests, fungal attack and dry or hot spells. The seller also says it improves nutrient uptake and transport, supports flowering, raises yield and helps detoxify problem soils.

The seller's listing gives a dose of 1.5 to 2 g per litre of water as a foliar spray, at any stage from vegetative growth to flowering and fruiting, and asks you to keep stirring the mixture while spraying. The listed crops are grapes, pomegranate, banana, ber, papaya, guava, coconut, arecanut, lime, sweet lime, orange, pineapple, fig, tea, coffee and spices. The shelf life is given as three years from the date of manufacture. Silicon supports the crop's own strength, but it does not replace a pesticide when pests or diseases are already present.

The seller's listing gives 1.5 to 2 g per litre of water as a foliar spray. Keep stirring the mixture while spraying.

7v9jM6B408EggXkHZcuu.description:
Pie Gen is an insecticide containing emamectin benzoate 5% SG (soluble granules), as stated on its label; the listing does not name the manufacturer. Emamectin benzoate 5% SG is used against lepidopteran pests, that is caterpillars, such as fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms and other leaf-eating larvae, in crops such as cotton, chilli, brinjal, okra and cabbage, depending on the crops on the label. It is most effective on young larvae, so spray at egg hatch or when the first feeding damage appears, rather than waiting for large caterpillars.

Caterpillars: fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms and other leaf-eating larvae.

When larvae are young, at egg hatch or at the first feeding damage. Older, larger caterpillars are harder to control.

Onekil is registered for onion. Dhanuka lists crabgrass (Digitaria sanguinalis) and nutgrass, or motha (Cyperus rotundus), among its targets, and says it controls most of the narrow-leaf and broadleaf weeds found in onion fields.

Dhanuka recommends 400 ml per acre in 150 litres of water, sprayed when the weeds are at the two to three leaf stage. Young weeds are much easier to kill, so do not wait for them to grow large.
