After the weeds have emerged, when they are at the two to three leaf stage.

Spray when mite colonies or whitefly nymphs first start building up, and cover the underside of the leaves well, since Oberon acts on contact and these pests live there. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period printed on the Bayer label. Mites (red spider mite, yellow mite, European red mite) and whiteflies, on the crops listed on the Bayer label.

ey1Lc3kH6NX3ZthuR5R0.description:
GOAL from Corteva Agriscience (formerly Dow AgroSciences) is a selective herbicide containing oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC. Oxyfluorfen blocks the PPO (protoporphyrinogen oxidase) enzyme. Spray on moist soil with a flat-fan nozzle, avoid disturbing the soil surface after a pre-emergence spray, and keep the spray off the leaves of sensitive non-target crops. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.a: Oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC.

faqs.q: In which crops can I use it?
faqs.a: Oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC is registered in India for onion, potato, groundnut, tea and direct-sown rice. Check the GOAL label for the crops approved for your pack.

faqs.q: Do I spray it before or after weeds come up?
faqs.a: It is used pre-emergence or very early post-emergence, depending on the crop. Follow the timing on the label.

Excel Mera 71 from Sumitomo Chemical India is a non-selective, systemic herbicide containing the ammonium salt of glyphosate at 71% in soluble granule (SG) form. It is sprayed on weeds that are already growing. The leaves absorb it and carry it through the plant to the roots, where it blocks the EPSPS enzyme that plants need to make essential amino acids, so the whole weed, including its underground parts, dies over the following days and weeks.

Sumitomo lists it for tea plantations and non-crop areas, which matches its registration in India. It controls annual and perennial grasses and broadleaf weeds, including hard-to-kill perennial grasses. Because it kills any green plant it reaches, it must not be sprayed on crops.

Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Excel Mera 71?
faqs.a: Sumitomo gives 6 to 10 g per litre of water. Follow the label for your weed situation.

faqs.q: Can I spray it in my crop?

faqs.a: When weeds are actively growing and about 6 to 8 inches tall, so there is enough leaf to absorb the herbicide.

elYYvpRQYDy7hLfO3Ehi.description:
Reeta is a hybrid (F1) bhindi (okra) seed sold under the Mahyco name. According to the seller's listing, it produces slender, shiny, dark green, tender pods about 10 to 11 cm long, on medium-dwarf plants with good vigour and branching. First picking usually starts about 45 to 50 days after sowing. The listing also reports tolerance to yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV), the most damaging viral disease of bhindi, and advises confirming the current claim on the seed packet.

The listing gives kharif and rabi as suitable seasons, subject to the local climate, and names Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh among suitable regions. Bhindi grows well in warm weather and in well-drained soil rich in organic matter; the seed germinates poorly in cold soil.

Pick the pods every two to three days while they are young and tender, since bhindi fruit turns fibrous quickly. Tolerance to YVMV does not mean immunity: control whitefly, which spreads the virus, and pull out infected plants early. As this is a hybrid, buy fresh seed each season.

faqs.a: About 45 to 50 days after sowing, according to the listing.

faqs.q: Is Reeta resistant to yellow vein mosaic?
faqs.a: The listing reports tolerance to YVMV. Tolerance reduces losses but does not make the plant immune, so keep whitefly under control and check the claim on the seed packet.

faqs.q: What do the pods look like?
faqs.a: Slender, shiny, dark green and tender, about 10 to 11 cm long.

faqs.q: Can I save seed from this crop?
faqs.a: No. It is an F1 hybrid, so saved seed will not give the same crop. Buy fresh seed each season.

1VJXcynYR3mqmtYdtxAJ.description:
Tata Metri from Rallis India, a Tata company, is a selective systemic herbicide containing metribuzin 70% WP (wettable powder). Metribuzin belongs to the triazinone group. It is absorbed by both the roots and the leaves of weeds and blocks photosystem II, the part of photosynthesis that captures light energy, so susceptible weeds turn yellow, dry from the leaf edges and die.

The seller's listing names soybean, wheat, potato, sugarcane and tomato. The target weeds listed include Phalaris minor (gulli danda) in wheat, Chenopodium album (bathua), Melilotus, Digitaria, Cyperus species, Borreria and Eragrostis. Depending on the crop, it is applied as a pre-emergence spray on moist soil or as an early post-emergence spray on young weeds, as the crop label specifies.

The seller's listing gives about 100 to 120 g per acre for wheat and 300 g per acre for soybean, potato and tomato. For sugarcane, follow the rate on the Rallis label. Soil type also matters: light, sandy soils with little organic matter need extra care, because the active moves faster and can injure the crop. Mix the powder into a little water first, then fill the tank. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. The pack size is 100 g.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Tata Metri?
faqs.a: Metribuzin 70% WP (wettable powder).

faqs.q: What is the dose for wheat?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives about 100 to 120 g per acre for wheat, mainly against Phalaris minor and broadleaf weeds. Check the Rallis label before use.

faqs.q: Should I spray before or after the weeds come up?
faqs.a: It works pre-emergence or early post-emergence, depending on the crop. Follow the timing on the label for your crop.

faqs.q: Does soil type affect how I use it?
faqs.a: Yes. On light, sandy soils the active moves faster and can harm the crop, so take extra care and follow the label advice for your soil.

Phule Sangam (KDS 726) is a soybean variety developed at the Agricultural Research Station, Kasbe Digraj, of Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Rahuri, in Maharashtra and released in 2016. Sow in kharif after the monsoon has set in; the listing suggests late June to early July, depending on rainfall and local advice. Treat the seed with a fungicide and Rhizobium culture before sowing and follow the seed rate on the bag. faqs.q: How many days does Phule Sangam take to mature?

EkEvXJaCdhqfC9mMfgjB.description:
The Alfa-8 Gold is a 20 litre battery-operated sprayer pump for farm use. It can be used to spray insecticides, fungicides, herbicides and foliar nutrients on field crops, vegetables and orchards, following the label of each product. The listing does not give the weight, dimensions, tank material or warranty, so ask the seller or check the box before buying.

For a long working life, charge the battery fully before first use and after each day's work, do not leave it fully drained for long periods, and rinse the tank, hose and nozzle with clean water after every use. Keep a separate sprayer for herbicides if you can, or wash it very thoroughly before using it on crops, since herbicide residue can damage them.

faqs.q: What is the tank capacity and battery?

faqs.q: Can I use it for herbicides?

faqs.q: How should I care for the battery?
faqs.a: Charge it fully after use with the supplied charger, avoid leaving it fully drained for long, and store the sprayer in a dry, shaded place.

TAG Quick Plus from Tropical Agrosystem is a selective, systemic post-emergence herbicide for grassy weeds. It contains quizalofop-ethyl 10% EC, from the aryloxyphenoxy-propionate group. The weed takes it in through its leaves and stems, and within about a day it moves through the plant to the growing points, where it blocks an enzyme (acetyl CoA carboxylase) that grasses need to make fats. The grass stops growing and then dries out over the following days.

Tropical Agrosystem lists soybean, cotton, groundnut, black gram and onion as crops. It controls narrow-leaf weeds such as Echinochloa (sawak), Eleusine (goosegrass), wild sorghum, Cynodon (doob grass), Saccharum (kans) and Johnson grass. It does not control broadleaf weeds or sedges, which need a different herbicide.

The manufacturer gives a dose of 180 ml per acre, sprayed on the foliage during the vegetative phase, preferably in the morning or evening, with a flat-fan or flood-jet nozzle. Spray while the grasses are young and actively growing. Keep the spray away from cereal crops such as maize, wheat, paddy and sorghum, which are grasses and will be damaged. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of TAG Quick Plus?
faqs.a: Tropical Agrosystem gives 180 ml per acre as a foliar spray.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use it in?
faqs.a: Soybean, cotton, groundnut, black gram and onion, as listed by Tropical Agrosystem.

U4VYD45pDWWgtd3mFbcY.description:
Rapigen is an insecticide containing chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (suspension concentrate), registered in India with the Central Insecticides Board. Chlorantraniliprole belongs to the diamide group. Caterpillars that eat treated leaves suffer an uncontrolled release of calcium in their muscles, stop feeding within hours and die over the next few days. It works mainly when eaten and also on contact, and it has a low impact on many beneficial insects, which makes it a good fit in IPM programmes.

The brand's product information lists it against stem borer and leaf folder in rice, diamondback moth in cabbage, American and spotted bollworms and tobacco caterpillar in cotton, fruit borer in tomato and chilli, and early shoot borer, top borer and termites in sugarcane. It is also listed for caterpillar pests in pulses such as pigeon pea, chickpea and soybean, and in crops such as maize, brinjal and okra.

Spray at the early larval stage, when eggs are hatching or the first feeding damage appears, with good coverage. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the label, and do not use diamide insecticides back to back; alternate with other groups. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. The listed pack is 300 ml.

faqs.a: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC, according to the brand's product information and registration details.
Caterpillar pests such as rice stem borer and leaf folder, diamondback moth, bollworms, tobacco caterpillar, fruit borers and sugarcane borers, plus termites in sugarcane.

faqs.q: Does it control sucking pests like whitefly?
faqs.a: No. It is meant for caterpillars and other chewing pests listed on the label.

Calaris Xtra from Syngenta is a selective, systemic herbicide for maize and sugarcane. It is a suspension concentrate (SC) combining mesotrione 2.27% w/w and atrazine 22.7% w/w. With two different modes of action, the mix controls both grassy and broadleaf weeds and also gives some residual control of weeds that germinate soon after spraying.

It is registered in India for maize and sugarcane, against weeds such as horse purslane (Trianthema), nutgrass (Cyperus), crabgrass (Digitaria sanguinalis), barnyard grass (Echinochloa), crowfoot grass (Dactyloctenium aegyptium) and Amaranthus.

The seller's listing gives 1,400 ml per acre in about 200 litres of water, sprayed after the weeds have emerged, at their three to four leaf stage. Spray evenly with a flat-fan nozzle when the soil has some moisture. Use it only in maize and sugarcane, and check the label before sowing a sensitive crop such as pulses or vegetables in the same field soon afterwards, because atrazine can persist in the soil. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Calaris Xtra?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives 1,400 ml per acre in about 200 litres of water. Follow the label for your crop.

Power Grow NPK 0:30:35 + Fe + TE is a fully water-soluble fertilizer with no nitrogen, 30% phosphorus (as P2O5) and 35% potassium (as K2O), plus iron (Fe) and trace elements (TE). High-phosphorus, high-potassium grades like this are mostly used from the pre-flowering stage onwards. Phosphorus supports roots, flowering and fruit set; potassium improves fruit size, colour, sweetness and keeping quality and helps the crop handle stress; and iron is needed for chlorophyll, helping against yellowing of young leaves. Because it has no nitrogen, it supports flowering and fruiting without pushing extra leafy growth. The seller lists it for all crops, including vegetables, fruits, field crops, pulses, oilseeds and plantation crops.

The seller's listing gives 3 to 5 g per litre of water for foliar spray, and 2.5 to 5 kg per acre through drip irrigation or drenching. Spray in the morning or evening, and do a small jar test before mixing with pesticides. Like other water-soluble fertilizers, it adds to the crop's main soil fertilizer programme rather than replacing it.

Atul lists weeds such as Commelina benghalensis, Cyperus iria, Digitaria sanguinalis, Echinochloa colona, Parthenium hysterophorus and Physalis minima. Atul launched Sindica in 2024.

Roundup 41 from Bayer is a systemic, non-selective herbicide containing glyphosate 41% SL (soluble liquid). Bayer lists Roundup for tea, for pre-plant use in rice fields, and for fallow land, plantations and non-cropped areas. The weeds on its list include Bermuda grass (doob), cogon grass (Imperata), jungle rice, cockspur grass, rice flat sedge, carpet grass and false daisy. Because it kills almost any green plant it touches, it must never be sprayed on a standing crop.

Spray when the weeds are actively growing and well leaved, using clean water and a flat-fan nozzle. Avoid spraying when rain is due within a few hours, and leave the weeds undisturbed for about a week so the chemical can move to the roots. Follow the dose and water volume on the Bayer label for each use. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources. Just before and during flowering, when the crop's need is highest, or as soon as deficiency signs appear.

Police from Gharda Chemicals is an insecticide that combines two actives, fipronil 40% and imidacloprid 40%, in a water-dispersible granule (WG). Gharda recommends Police for the control of white grubs in sugarcane and groundnut. White grubs live in the soil and feed on roots, so they are hard to reach with ordinary sprays. Check the label for the full list of crops and pests it is registered for, and the method of application for each.

Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

This combination is registered in India for diseases such as anthracnose and powdery mildew in chilli, early and late blight in tomato, and blast and sheath blight in paddy, among other crops on its label. Use it only on the crops printed on the pack.

Spray at the first signs of disease, or as a protective spray when the weather favours infection, and cover the plant thoroughly. Follow the dose and waiting period on the label, and do not use strobilurin fungicides more often in a season than the label allows, to slow resistance. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

Spray at the first spindle-shaped blast spots on the leaves, or as a protective spray when the weather is cloudy and humid with heavy dew, and cover the crop well. Use the dose, water volume and waiting period on the label. If you grow basmati for export, check with your buyer or local agriculture office first, because some markets set very strict residue limits for tricyclazole. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

Poorva Chelmix-Combi is a water-soluble micronutrient mixture from Poorva Chemtech, made for foliar spraying. The listing does not give the breakdown of elements, so check the pouch for which micronutrients it contains and in what amounts.

Multi-micronutrient sprays are used to correct or prevent deficiencies that show as yellowing between the veins of young leaves, small or narrow leaves, or poor flowering and fruit set. Such deficiencies are common in alkaline, calcareous or intensively cropped soils. The listing names tomato, onion, capsicum, brinjal, cauliflower, grapes, pomegranate, banana, mango, sugarcane, cotton and cereals, and says it suits all soil types.

The seller's listing gives 1.5 to 2 g per litre of water but also asks buyers to verify the dose on the back of the pouch, and some published directions for this product give a lower rate, so go by the pouch. faqs.q: What is the dose of Chelmix-Combi?

eeaFVAxpYGuUVTj9CfbX.description:
CombiFert Liquid is a liquid micronutrient mixture for spraying on the leaves. According to the label composition given in the seller's listing, it contains iron (Fe) 2.5%, manganese (Mn) 1%, zinc (Zn) 3%, boron (B) 0.5%, copper (Cu) 1% and molybdenum (Mo) 0.1%, with the metals chelated with EDTA. Crops need these six elements only in small amounts, but a shortage of any one of them can hold back growth even when nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are sufficient. Typical signs are yellowing between the veins of new leaves (often iron or manganese), small, narrow or bunched leaves (zinc), and poor flowering and fruit set (boron). Chelation with EDTA protects the metal so that it stays in a form the plant can take up instead of reacting with other salts. A foliar spray reaches the leaf directly, which is useful in alkaline or calcareous soils where micronutrients get locked up.

Spray it during active vegetative growth and before flowering, or when deficiency signs first appear. The listing does not give a dose, so use the rate on the pack. Do a small jar test before mixing it with pesticides, and spray in the cooler part of the day. This listing is a 1 litre pack.

faqs.q: Which nutrients does CombiFert Liquid contain?
faqs.a: Fe 2.5%, Mn 1%, Zn 3%, B 0.5%, Cu 1% and Mo 0.1%, according to the label composition in the listing.

Nexa NPK 00:09:46 is a 100% water-soluble mixture fertilizer. The grade means it contains no nitrogen, 9% phosphorus (as P2O5) and 46% potassium (as K2O), and the seller adds that it is enriched with sulphur and is free of sodium and chlorine. A high-potash, low-phosphorus fertilizer like this is used from flowering onwards, when the crop needs potassium most. Potassium moves sugars into fruits, bulbs, tubers and grains, so it supports size, colour, sweetness, firmness and keeping quality. It also helps the plant manage water loss and cope better with dry spells. The small amount of phosphorus supports flowering and root activity, and sulphur helps with protein and oil formation in crops such as onion, garlic and oilseeds. Being free of chlorine and sodium makes it suitable for crops that are sensitive to them and for use through drip systems.

Because it dissolves completely, it can be applied through drip irrigation or sprayed on the leaves. Dissolve it fully in clean water before use, and follow the dose and crop stage given on the pack.

Phosphorus and potassium are the nutrients crops lean on most from flowering onwards. Phosphorus supports root activity, energy transfer inside the plant, flowering and the formation of seeds and fruit. Potassium helps fruit and grain fill, supports size, colour and quality, strengthens stems and helps the plant cope with dry spells. Iron keeps new leaves green and is needed to make chlorophyll. Because there is no nitrogen, a product like this suits the reproductive stage, when the aim is more flowers, fruit and grain rather than more leaves.

As a water-soluble fertilizer it can be given through drip or as a foliar spray, usually from flower initiation through fruit development. Tynzer from BASF is a selective post-emergence herbicide for maize. It contains topramezone 336 g per litre (33.6% w/v) in a suspension concentrate (SC). Treated weeds turn white (bleach), stop growing and die over the following days. Maize can break the chemical down, which is why it can be sprayed over the crop.

Tynzer controls both grassy and broadleaf weeds in maize. The seller lists grasses such as Eleusine indica, Digitaria sanguinalis, Echinochloa and Dactyloctenium aegyptium, and broadleaf weeds such as Parthenium (gajar ghas), Amaranthus viridis (chaulai), Digera arvensis, Convolvulus arvensis (hirankhuri) and Celosia argentea. Spray early, when the grasses are 2 to 3 inches tall and the broadleaf weeds are at the 2 to 3 leaf stage, on moist soil.

The seller's listing gives 30 ml per acre (3 to 4 ml per 15 litre pump) mixed with an MSO adjuvant at 2 ml per litre (about 300 ml per acre), in 150 to 200 litres of water, with a flat-fan nozzle and a maximum of one spray per season. Avoid spraying if rain is expected within 2 hours. Keep it away from ponds and streams. Read the label, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep the product away from children, food and water sources.

Combining two modes of action in one spray gives broader control of sucking pests such as aphids, jassids and thrips, and helps where a single insecticide no longer works well. Use it only on the crops and pests printed on the label, since the registered uses decide where it can be applied.

Shake the bottle well before use, mix the measured dose into a little water, then fill the tank and spray for good coverage, including the underside of the leaves. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the label. Fipronil is highly toxic to bees and fish, so do not spray during flowering when bees are active, and never wash the pump in ponds or streams. treT0rdk0EvXl4qMjvjb.description:
Score from Syngenta is a systemic fungicide containing difenoconazole 25% EC (emulsifiable concentrate). Difenoconazole is a triazole. Spray at the first signs of disease, or before it appears when the weather favours it, and cover the crop well. Use the dose, water volume and waiting period on the label. Rotate Score with fungicides from other groups instead of spraying it again and again, so that the fungus does not build up resistance. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

Maharaza is a mycorrhizal biofertilizer, which makes it a living microbial product rather than a chemical stimulant. The brand describes it as built on microbiome selection and Bio-Mimic technology for stronger root development, and recommends it for all crops. The listing does not give the fungus species or spore count, so check the pack for these details.

Mycorrhizal fungi attach to plant roots and grow fine threads (hyphae) out into the soil, acting like a second root system. These threads reach water and nutrients, especially phosphorus, beyond the zone the roots themselves can explore, and pass them to the plant in exchange for sugars. The brand lists benefits such as a larger root surface area, better soil structure, better moisture holding under stress, and support for germination and early growth.

Apply it to the soil near the root zone, by broadcasting or by banding along the rows, ideally at sowing or transplanting or early in the crop, so the fungi can colonise young roots. The brand states it is compatible with fertilizers, insecticides and biostimulants; avoid mixing it directly with fungicides, which can harm living fungi. Use the dose on the pack, use the contents soon after opening, and store unopened packs in a cool, shaded place.

faqs.q: What kind of product is Maharaza?
faqs.a: A mycorrhizal biofertilizer: beneficial fungi that live on roots and help the crop take up water and nutrients.
To the soil at the root zone, by broadcasting or banding, preferably at sowing, transplanting or early in the crop. Use the dose on the pack.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with fertilizers or insecticides?
faqs.a: The brand says it is compatible with fertilizers, insecticides and biostimulants. Keep fungicides separate, as they can harm the fungi.

faqs.q: Does it add phosphorus to the soil?
faqs.a: No. It adds no phosphorus itself; it helps roots reach and take up the phosphorus already in the soil or applied as fertilizer.

Nativo from Bayer is a broad-spectrum fungicide containing tebuconazole 50% and trifloxystrobin 25% as water-dispersible granules (WG). Trifloxystrobin is a strobilurin that binds to the waxy surface of the leaf and spreads over and into it (mesostemic action), forming a protective layer that stops fungal spores from germinating. Tebuconazole is a systemic triazole that moves inside the plant and stops infections that have already begun. Together they give protective and curative action and lower the risk of resistance.

In India, tebuconazole 50% + trifloxystrobin 25% WG is registered for rice (sheath blight, leaf and neck blast and grain discolouration), tomato (early blight), chilli (powdery mildew, anthracnose and Alternaria leaf spot), wheat (yellow rust and powdery mildew), grapes (powdery mildew) and mango (powdery mildew and anthracnose).

The seller's listing gives 0.5 to 1 g per litre of water, or 80 to 120 g per acre depending on the crop; the label sets the exact rate for each crop. Mix the granules in a little water first, then add to the tank, and spray at the early stage of disease with full cover of the crop. Read the label before use, wear gloves and a mask, do not spray against the wind, and keep it away from children, food and water sources.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Nativo?

faqs.q: When should I spray Nativo in rice?

faqs.q: How many times can I spray it?
faqs.a: Follow the maximum number of sprays on the label and alternate with fungicides from other groups.

Dayal Borofert 20 is a boron fertilizer sold under the Dayal brand. According to the seller's listing, it contains 20% boron in the form of disodium octaborate tetrahydrate. This form of boron dissolves readily in water, so it can be sprayed on the leaves or applied through drip irrigation or to the soil.

Boron is a micronutrient that crops need in very small amounts but cannot do without. It is needed for building cell walls, for the growth of root and shoot tips, and above all for flowering, pollen growth and fruit or seed set. A shortage shows as poor flowering, flower and fruit drop, cracked or hollow stems and fruits, small or misshapen fruits, and death of growing tips. Deficiency is common in sandy, alkaline and low-organic-matter soils, and in crops that need more boron, such as cotton, groundnut, sunflower, cauliflower, grapes, pomegranate and papaya.

The seller lists it for all crops but gives its dose figure without a unit, so use the rate printed on the pack. Do not overdose: the gap between enough boron and too much is narrow, and excess boron can scorch leaves and damage the crop. Packs of 100 g, 250 g, 500 g and 1 kg are available.

faqs.a: Boron 20% as disodium octaborate tetrahydrate, according to the listing.

faqs.q: What are the signs of boron deficiency?
faqs.a: Poor flowering, flower and fruit drop, cracked or hollow stems and fruits, small or misshapen fruits, and dying growing tips.
The listing gives a figure of 1 to 1.5 without a unit, so follow the rate on the pack. Too much boron can damage the crop.
